strengths: The shared construction for random forests and ReLU networks is interesting and relevant to researchers studying uncertainty estimation. Reusing learned partitions for post-hoc confidence adjustment without OOD training examples offers a useful practical direction.

For a fixed fitted model with positive, finite Gaussian variances and a positive density floor, Proposition 2 establishes an interpretable result: predictions approach the empirical class priors as distance from the training data increases.

The experiments cover six synthetic problems, 45 tabular datasets, and vision models using two encoder architectures. Synthetic posterior comparisons, Euclidean-versus-geodesic comparisons, and individual dataset results provide useful evidence beyond aggregate accuracy.

The reported results demonstrate promising confidence–accuracy tradeoffs. In Table 1, KDN reduces CIFAR-100 OCE from 0.47 to 0.12 while CIFAR-10 accuracy changes from 98.06% to 97.45%. The equations and posterior visualizations help communicate the mechanism.
weaknesses: Necessary: The central calibration claims exceed what the evaluation establishes. Equation (1) prescribes the training prior outside a high-density region; this is a chosen fallback, not an established OOD conditional label distribution. OCE in Equation (18) measures only agreement between maximum probabilities. With priors (0.9, 0.1), predictions (0.1, 0.9) receive zero OCE despite violating the stated target. Distinguish prior reversion from statistical calibration, evaluate the full probability vector when testing Equation (1), and either support OOD detection claims with detection metrics or narrow those claims.

Necessary: State the limits of Proposition 2 explicitly. It concerns distance tending to infinity for a fixed model, and does not establish behavior throughout the finite OOD region. In the vision experiments, Gaussian fitting occurs in encoder space; distant or unfamiliar images need not have distant embeddings. The theorem therefore does not provide an input-space guarantee for these systems without additional assumptions. Restrict the guarantee to the space and limiting regime actually covered.

Necessary: Correct or qualify the probabilistic interpretation. Piecewise-affine ReLU logits are not class-conditional densities and can be negative, contrary to Equation (3)'s interpretation. Moreover, nearest-component selection does not preserve classwise density normalization, and adding b/log(n) makes the resulting functions nonintegrable over R^D. Equation (7) still defines valid normalized predictive scores, but its interpretation as Bayes inference from estimated class-conditional densities requires justification. Presenting the method as a confidence-shrinkage rule would avoid this unsupported interpretation.

Necessary: Important experimental details are missing: the search range and objective for k, baseline tuning settings, OE exposure data, training schedules, precise train/calibration/test splits, repetition counts, and definitions of the reported uncertainty intervals. These omissions prevent confident assessment of the comparisons, particularly the broad assertion that OOD methods degrade ID calibration. Report sufficient precision for Table 1's MCE values and limit comparative conclusions to the evaluated configurations.

Necessary: Resolve discrepancies affecting reproducibility. Algorithms 2–3 omit the exponentiation specified in Equation (15), and Algorithm 1 describes grouping by 'similar weight' without specifying the exact polytope equivalence. Equation (10) places the variance regularizer inside the sum over all training samples, producing a floor of nλ/n_r; clarify whether this is intended. Appendix C also specifies identical Gaussian mixtures for both XOR classes, inconsistent with the displayed experiment.

Optional: Ablations of the density floor and count smoothing, together with a simple density-based prior-shrinkage baseline, would clarify which components explain the gains. Runtime and memory measurements would also help readers assess practicality, given the quadratic pairwise pseudocode and the apparently exponential activation-path representation.
